text: The World Health Organization's 2024 Global Health Report found that life expectancy in sub-Saharan Africa increased by 2.4 years between 2015 and 2023, driven primarily by expanded access to antiretroviral therapy and improved maternal healthcare. However, the report also noted that progress has been uneven. Countries affected by armed conflict, such as South Sudan and the Democratic Republic of Congo, saw stagnant or declining life expectancy during the same period. The authors recommend sustained investment in primary care infrastructure and conflict-sensitive health programming.
